stem: Find the derivative of \(x^{n}\) w. r. t. \(x\) for \(n \in N\).
solution:
Let \(f(x) = x^{n}\)
\(f(x+h) = (x+h)^{n}\)
By method of first principle,
\(f'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h}\right)\)
\(f'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{(x+h)^{n}-x^{n}}{h}\right)\)
\(= \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{x^{n} + {}^{n}C_{1}x^{n-1}h + {}^{n}C_{2}x^{n-2}h^{2} + \ldots\ldots + h^{n} - x^{n}}{h}\right)\)
\(= \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{{}^{n}C_{1}x^{n-1}h + {}^{n}C_{2}x^{n-2}h^{2} + {}^{n}C_{3}x^{n-3}h^{3} + \ldots\ldots + h^{n}}{h}\right)\)
\(= \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{h\left({}^{n}C_{1}x^{n-1} + {}^{n}C_{2}x^{n-2}h + {}^{n}C_{3}x^{n-3}h^{2} + \ldots\ldots + h^{n-1}\right)}{h}\right)\)
\(= \lim_{h \to 0}\left(nx^{n-1} + {}^{n}C_{2}x^{n-2}h + {}^{n}C_{3}x^{n-3}h^{2} + \ldots\ldots + h^{n-1}\right)\)
\(= nx^{n-1} + 0 + 0 + \ldots + 0\)  (as \(h \to 0\), \(h \ne 0\))
\(\therefore\) if \(f(x) = x^{n}\), \(f'(x) = nx^{n-1}\)

stem: Find derivative of \(\sin x\) w. r. t. \(x\).
solution:
Let \(f(x) = \sin x\)
\(f(x+h) = \sin(x+h)\)
By method of first principle,
\(f'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h}\right)\)
\(f'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{\sin(x+h)-\sin x}{h}\right)\)
\(= \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{2\cos\left(\frac{2x+h}{2}\right)\cdot\sin\left(\frac{h}{2}\right)}{h}\right)\)
\(= 2\lim_{h \to 0}\cos\left(\frac{2x+h}{2}\right)\lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{\sin\left(\frac{h}{2}\right)}{\frac{h}{2}}\right)\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\)
\(= 2\lim_{h \to 0}\cos\left(x+\frac{h}{2}\right)\lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{\sin\left(\frac{h}{2}\right)}{\frac{h}{2}}\right)\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\)
\(= 2\cos x\cdot(1)\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\) \(\ldots\ldots\) \(\left[\because \lim_{\theta \to 0}\left(\frac{\sin p\theta}{p\theta}\right) = 1\right]\)
\(\therefore\) if \(f(x) = \sin x\), \(f'(x) = \cos x\)
_note: In the printed final line the prime mark on \(f'(x)\) appears DOUBLED (reads as \(f''(x)\)) — every sibling example on the same spread prints a single prime. Transcribed here as \(f'(x)\); a typesetting slip, not answer-affecting (the stated result \(\cos x\) is the first derivative and matches the derivation above it).

stem: Find the derivative of \(\tan x\) w. r. t. \(x\).
solution:
Let \(f(x) = \tan x\)
\(f(x+h) = \tan(x+h)\)
From the definition,
\(f'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h}\right)\)
\(f'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{\tan(x+h)-\tan x}{h}\right)\)
\(= \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{\frac{\sin(x+h)}{\cos(x+h)} - \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}}{h}\right)\)
\(= \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{\frac{\sin(x+h)\cdot\cos x - \cos(x+h)\sin x}{\cos(x+h)\cdot\cos x}}{h}\right)\)
\(= \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{\sin h}{h\cdot\cos(x+h)\cdot\cos x}\right)\)
\(= \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{\sin h}{h}\right)\cdot\lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{1}{\cos(x+h)\cdot\cos x}\right)\)
\(= (1)\cdot\left(\frac{1}{\cos^{2}x}\right)\) \(\ldots\ldots\) \(\left[\because \lim_{\theta \to 0}\left(\frac{\sin\theta}{\theta}\right) = 1\right]\)
\(\therefore\) if \(f(x) = \tan x\), \(f'(x) = \sec^{2}x\)

stem: Find the derivative of \(\sec x\) w. r. t. \(x\).
solution:
Let \(f(x) = \sec x\)
\(f(x+h) = \sec(x+h)\)
From the definition,
\(f'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h}\right)\)
\(f'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{\sec(x+h)-\sec x}{h}\right)\)
\(= \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{\frac{1}{\cos(x+h)} - \frac{1}{\cos x}}{h}\right)\)
\(= \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{\frac{\cos x - \cos(x+h)}{\cos(x+h)\cdot\cos x}}{h}\right)\)
\(= \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{-2\sin\left(\frac{2x+h}{2}\right)\cdot\sin\left(\frac{-h}{2}\right)}{h\cdot\cos(x+h)\cdot\cos x}\right)\)
\(= 2\lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{\sin\left(\frac{2x+h}{2}\right)}{\cos(x+h)\cdot\cos x}\right)\lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{\sin\left(\frac{h}{2}\right)}{\frac{h}{2}}\right)\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\)
\(= \frac{2\sin x}{\cos^{2}x}\cdot(1)\cdot\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\) \(\ldots\ldots\) \(\left[\because \lim_{\theta \to 0}\left(\frac{\sin p\theta}{p\theta}\right) = 1\right]\)
\(\therefore\) if \(f(x) = \sec x\), \(f'(x) = \sec x\,\tan x\)

stem: Find the derivative of \(\log x\) w. r. t. \(x\). \((x > 0)\)
solution:
Let \(f(x) = \log x\)
\(f(x+h) = \log(x+h)\)
From the definition,
\(f'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h}\right)\)
\(f'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{\log(x+h)-\log(x)}{h}\right)\)
\(= \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{\log\left(\frac{x+h}{x}\right)}{h}\right)\)
\(= \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{\log\left(1+\frac{h}{x}\right)}{h}\right)\)
\(= \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{\log\left(1+\frac{h}{x}\right)}{\frac{h}{x}}\right)\times\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)\)
\(= 1\cdot\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)\) \(\left[\because \lim_{x \to 0}\left(\frac{\log(1+x)}{x}\right) = 1\right]\)
\(\therefore\) if \(f(x) = \log x\), \(f'(x) = \frac{1}{x}\)

stem: Find then derivative of \(a^{x}\) w. r. t. \(x\). \((a > 0)\)
solution:
Let \(f(x) = a^{x}\)
\(f(x+h) = a^{x+h}\)
From the definition,
\(f'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h}\right)\)
\(f'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{a^{(x+h)}-a^{x}}{h}\right)\)
\(= \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{a^{x}\left(a^{h}-1\right)}{h}\right)\)
\(= a^{x}\lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{a^{h}-1}{h}\right)\)
\(f'(x) = a^{x}\log a\) \(\ldots\ldots\) \(\left[\because \lim_{x \to 0}\left(\frac{a^{x}-1}{x}\right) = \log a\right]\)
\(\therefore\) if \(f(x) = a^{x}\), \(f'(x) = a^{x}\cdot\log a\)
_note: Stem transcribed as printed: the book prints "Find then derivative of" — "then" is a misprint for "the". Not answer-affecting.

subtopic: Derivative by the Method of First Principle
context: Find the derivatives of the following from the definition,
solution:
Let \(f(x) = \sqrt{x}\)
\(f(x+h) = \sqrt{x+h}\)
From the definition,
\(f'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h}\right)\)
\(f'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{\sqrt{x+h}-\sqrt{x}}{h}\right)\)
\(= \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{\sqrt{x+h}-\sqrt{x}}{h}\times\frac{\sqrt{x+h}+\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{x+h}+\sqrt{x}}\right)\)
\(= \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{x+h-x}{h\left(\sqrt{x+h}+\sqrt{x}\right)}\right)\)
\(= \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{h}{h\left(\sqrt{x+h}+\sqrt{x}\right)}\right)\)
\(= \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{x+h}+\sqrt{x}}\right)\) \(\ldots\)[As \(h \to 0\), \(h \ne 0\)]
\(= \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\)

subtopic: Derivative by the Method of First Principle
context: Find the derivatives of the following from the definition,
solution:
Let \(f(x) = \cos(2x+3)\)
\(f(x+h) = \cos(2(x+h)+3) = \cos((2x+3)+2h)\)
From the definition,
\(f'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h}\right)\)
\(f'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{\cos[(2x+3)+2h]-\cos(2x+3)}{h}\right)\)
\(= \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{-2\sin\left(\frac{2(2x+3)+2h}{2}\right)\sin(h)}{h}\right)\)
\(= \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{-2\sin(2x+3+h)\sin(h)}{h}\right)\)
\(= \lim_{h \to 0}\left[-2\sin(2x+3+h)\right]\lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{\sin h}{h}\right)\)
\(= \left[-2\sin(2x+3)\right](1)\) \(\ldots\ldots\) \(\left[\because \lim_{\theta \to 0}\left(\frac{\sin\theta}{\theta}\right) = 1\right]\)
\(= -2\sin(2x+3)\)

subtopic: Derivative by the Method of First Principle
context: Find the derivatives of the following from the definition,
solution:
Let \(f(x) = 4^{x}\)
\(f(x+h) = 4^{x+h}\)
From the definition
\(f'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h}\right)\)
\(f'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{4^{x+h}-4^{x}}{h}\right)\)
\(= \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{4^{x}\left(4^{h}-1\right)}{h}\right)\)
\(= 4^{x}\lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{4^{h}-1}{h}\right)\)
\(= 4^{x}\log 4\) \(\ldots\ldots\) \(\left[\because \lim_{x \to 0}\left(\frac{a^{x}-1}{x}\right) = \log a\right]\)

subtopic: Derivative by the Method of First Principle
context: Find the derivatives of the following from the definition,
solution:
Let \(f(x) = \log(3x-2)\)
\(f(x+h) = \log[3(x+h)-2] = \log[(3x-2)+3h]\)
From the definition,
\(f'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h}\right)\)
\(f'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{\log[(3x-2)+3h]-\log(3x-2)}{h}\right)\)
\(= \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{\log\left(\frac{(3x-2)+3h}{3x-2}\right)}{h}\right)\)
\(= \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{\log\left(1+\frac{3h}{3x-2}\right)}{h}\right)\)
\(= \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{\log\left(1+\frac{3h}{3x-2}\right)}{\frac{3h}{3x-2}}\right)\times\left(\frac{3}{3x-2}\right)\)
\(= (1)\times\left(\frac{3}{3x-2}\right)\) \(\left[\because \lim_{x \to 0}\left(\frac{\log(1+px)}{px}\right) = 1\right]\)
\(= \frac{3}{3x-2}\)

subtopic: Derivative by the Method of First Principle
stem: Find the derivative of \(f(x) = \sin x\), at \(x = \pi\)
solution:
\(f(x) = \sin x\)
\(f(\pi) = \sin \pi = 0\)
\(f(\pi+h) = \sin(\pi+h) = -\sin h\)
From the definition,
\(f'(a) = \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{f(a+h)-f(a)}{h}\right)\)
\(f'(\pi) = \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{f(\pi+h)-f(\pi)}{h}\right)\)
\(= \lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{-\sin h - 0}{h}\right) = \lim_{h \to 0}\left(-\frac{\sin h}{h}\right)\)
\(= -\lim_{h \to 0}\left(\frac{\sin h}{h}\right)\)
\(= -1\) \(\left[\because \lim_{\theta \to 0}\left(\frac{\sin\theta}{\theta}\right) = 1\right]\)

subtopic: Derivative by the Method of First Principle
Definition of the Derivative and Differentiability
stem: Test whether the function \(f(x)=(3x-2)^{\frac{2}{5}}\) is differentiable at \(x=\frac{2}{3}\).
solution:
Given that, \(f(x)=(3x-2)^{\frac{2}{5}}\)

\(f'(a)=\lim_{h\to 0}\left(\frac{f(a+h)-f(a)}{h}\right)\)

Note that \(f\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)=0\)

For \(x=\frac{2}{3}\), \(f'\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)=\lim_{h\to 0}\left(\frac{f\left(\frac{2}{3}+h\right)-f\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)}{h}\right)\)

\(=\lim_{h\to 0}\left(\frac{\left[3\left(\frac{2}{3}+h\right)-2\right]^{\frac{2}{5}}}{h}\right)\)

\(=\lim_{h\to 0}\left(\frac{[2+3h-2]^{\frac{2}{5}}}{h}\right)\)

\(=\lim_{h\to 0}\left(\frac{(3h)^{\frac{2}{5}}}{h}\right)=3^{\frac{2}{5}}\lim_{h\to 0}\left(\frac{h^{\frac{2}{5}}}{h}\right)\)

\(=3^{\frac{2}{5}}\lim_{h\to 0}\left(\frac{1}{h^{\frac{3}{5}}}\right)\)

This limit does not exist.

\(\therefore f(x)\) is not differentiable at \(x=\frac{2}{3}\).

subtopic: Definition of the Derivative and Differentiability
solution:
Given that \(f(x)=(x-2)|x-2|\)

That is \(f(x)=-(x-2)^2\) for \(x<2\)

\(\quad\quad\quad\;\; =(x-2)^2\) for \(x\ge 2\)

\(Lf'(2)=\lim_{h\to 0^-}\left(\frac{f(2+h)-f(2)}{h}\right)\)

\(=\lim_{h\to 0^-}\left(\frac{-(2+h-2)^2-(2-2)^2}{h}\right)\)

\(=\lim_{h\to 0^-}\left(\frac{-h^2}{h}\right)=\lim_{h\to 0^-}(-h)\)

\(Lf'(2)=0\)

\(Rf'(2)=\lim_{h\to 0^+}\left(\frac{f(2+h)-f(2)}{h}\right)\)

\(=\lim_{h\to 0^+}\left(\frac{(2+h-2)^2-(2-2)^2}{h}\right)\)

\(=\lim_{h\to 0^+}\left(\frac{h^2}{h}\right)=\lim_{h\to 0^+}(h)\)

\(Rf'(2)=0\)

So, \(Lf'(2)=Rf'(2)=0\)

Hence the function \(f(x)\) is differentiable at \(x=2\).

stem:
Show the function \(f(x)\) is continuous at \(x=3\), but not differentiable at \(x=3\). if

\(f(x)=2x+1\) for \(x\le 3\)

\(\quad\quad\;\; =16-x^2\) for \(x>3\).
solution:
\(f(x)=2x+1\) for \(x\le 3\)

\(\quad\quad\;\; =16-x^2\) for \(x>3\).

For \(x=3\), \(f(3)=2(3)+1=7\)

\(\lim_{x\to 3^-}f(x)=\lim_{x\to 3}(2x+1)=2(3)+1=7\)

\(\lim_{x\to 3^+}f(x)=\lim_{x\to 3}(16-x^2)=16-(3)^2=7\)

\(\lim_{x\to 3^-}f(x)=\lim_{x\to 3^+}f(x)=f(3)=7\)

\(\therefore f(x)\) is continuous at \(x=3\).

\(Lf'(3)=\lim_{h\to 0^-}\left(\frac{f(3+h)-f(3)}{h}\right)\)

\(=\lim_{h\to 0}\left(\frac{2(3+h)+1-7}{h}\right)\)

\(=\lim_{h\to 0}\left(\frac{6+2h+1-7}{h}\right)\)

\(=\lim_{h\to 0}\left(\frac{2h}{h}\right)=\lim_{h\to 0}(2)\)

\(Lf'(3)=2\) ................. (1)

\(Rf'(3)=\lim_{h\to 0^+}\left(\frac{f(3+h)-f(3)}{h}\right)\)

\(=\lim_{h\to 0}\left(\frac{16-(3+h)^2-7}{h}\right)=\lim_{h\to 0}\left(\frac{16-9-6h-h^2-7}{h}\right)\)

\(=\lim_{h\to 0}\left(\frac{-h(6+h)}{h}\right)=\lim_{h\to 0}(-(6+h))\)

\(Rf'(3)=-6\) ................. (2)

from (1) and (2), \(Lf'(3)\ne Rf'(3)\)

\(\therefore f(x)\) is not differentiable at \(x=3\).

Hence \(f(x)\) is continuous at \(x=3\), but not differentiable at \(x=3\).

subtopic: Definition of the Derivative and Differentiability
stem: Show that the function \(f(x)\) is differentiable at \(x=-3\) where, \(f(x)=x^2+2\).
solution:
For \(x=-3\), \(f'(-3)=\lim_{h\to 0}\left(\frac{f(-3+h)-f(-3)}{h}\right)\)

\(=\lim_{h\to 0}\left(\frac{(-3+h)^2+2-11}{h}\right)\)

\(=\lim_{h\to 0}\left(\frac{9-6h+h^2+2-11}{h}\right)\)

\(=\lim_{h\to 0}\left(\frac{h^2-6h}{h}\right)\)

\(=\lim_{h\to 0}(h-6)\quad(\because h\to 0,\ h\ne 0)\)

\(=-6\)

\(f'(-3)\) exists so, \(f(x)\) is differentiable at \(x=-3\).

context: Find the derivatives of the following functions
solution:
Given, \(y=x^{\frac{3}{2}}+\log x-\cos x\)

Differentiate w.r.t.x.

\(\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{d}{dx}\left(x^{\frac{3}{2}}+\log x-\cos x\right)\)

\(=\frac{d}{dx}\left(x^{\frac{3}{2}}\right)+\frac{d}{dx}(\log x)-\frac{d}{dx}(\cos x)\)

\(=\frac{3}{2}x^{\frac{1}{2}}+\frac{1}{x}-(-\sin x)\)

\(\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{3}{2}\sqrt{x}+\frac{1}{x}+\sin x\)

context: Find the derivatives of the following functions
solution:
Given \(f(x)=x^5\operatorname{cosec}x+\sqrt{x}\tan x\)

Differentiate w.r.t.x.

\(f'(x)=\frac{d}{dx}\left(x^5\operatorname{cosec}x+\sqrt{x}\tan x\right)\)

\(=\frac{d}{dx}\left(x^5\operatorname{cosec}x\right)+\frac{d}{dx}\left(\sqrt{x}\tan x\right)\)

\(=x^5\times\frac{d}{dx}(\operatorname{cosec}x)+\operatorname{cosec}x\times\frac{d}{dx}(x^5)+\sqrt{x}\times\frac{d}{dx}(\tan x)+\tan x\times\frac{d}{dx}\sqrt{x}\)

\(=x^5\times(-\operatorname{cosec}x\times\cot x)+\operatorname{cosec}x\times(5x^4)+\sqrt{x}\times(\sec^2 x)+\tan x\times\left(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\right)\)

\(=-x^5\operatorname{cosec}x.\cot x+5x^4\operatorname{cosec}x+\sqrt{x}\times(\sec^2 x)+\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\tan x\)

context: Find the derivatives of the following functions
solution:
Given that \(y=\left(\frac{e^x-5}{e^x+5}\right)\)

Differentiate w.r.t.x.

\(\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{e^x-5}{e^x+5}\right)\)

\(=\frac{(e^x+5)\times\frac{d}{dx}(e^x-5)-(e^x-5)\times\frac{d}{dx}(e^x+5)}{(e^x+5)^2}\)

\(=\frac{(e^x+5).(e^x)-(e^x-5).(e^x)}{(e^x+5)^2}\)

\(=\frac{e^{2x}+5(e^x)-e^{2x}+5(e^x)}{(e^x+5)^2}\)

\(=\frac{10e^x}{(e^x+5)^2}\)

context: Find the derivatives of the following functions
solution:
\(y=\frac{x\sin x}{x+\sin x}\)

Differentiate w.r.t.x.,

\(\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{x\sin x}{x+\sin x}\right)\)

\(=\frac{(x+\sin x)\times\frac{d}{dx}(x\sin x)-(x\sin x)\times\frac{d}{dx}(x+\sin x)}{(x+\sin x)^2}\)

\(=\frac{(x+\sin x)\times\left(x\frac{d}{dx}(\sin x)+\sin x\frac{d}{dx}(x)\right)-(x\sin x).(1+\cos x)}{(x+\sin x)^2}\)

\(=\frac{(x+\sin x).(x\cos x+\sin x)-(x\sin x).(1+\cos x)}{(x+\sin x)^2}\)

\(=\frac{x^2\cos x+x\sin x+x\sin x\cos x+\sin^2 x-x\sin x-x\sin x\cos x}{(x+\sin x)^2}\)

\(=\frac{x^2\cos x+\sin^2 x}{(x+\sin x)^2}\)

stem: If \(f(x)=p\tan x+q\sin x+r\), \(f(0)=-4\sqrt{3}\), \(f\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=-7\sqrt{3}\), \(f'\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=3\) then find \(p\), \(q\) and \(r\).
solution:
Given that \(f(x)=p\tan x+q\sin x+r\) ...(1)

\(f'(x)=p\sec^2 x+q\cos x\) ...(2)

\(f(0)=-4\sqrt{3}\)

put \(x=0\) in (1)

\(f(0)=p\tan 0+q\sin 0+r=r\) \(\therefore r=-4\sqrt{3}\)

\(f\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=-7\sqrt{3}\),

\(\therefore\) from (1) \(p\tan\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)+q\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)+r=-7\sqrt{3}\)

\(p\sqrt{3}+q\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-4\sqrt{3}=-7\sqrt{3}\) \(\therefore 2p+q=-6\) ...(3)

\(f'\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=3\)

\(\therefore\) from (2), \(p\sec^2\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)+q\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=3\)

\(4p+\frac{q}{2}=3\) \(\therefore 8p+q=6\) ...(4)

(4) \(-\) (3) gives \(6p=12\) \(\therefore p=2\), put \(p=2\) in (3), we get \(q=-10\) \(\therefore p=2\), \(q=-10\) and \(r=-4\sqrt{3}\)

_note: BOOK DEFECT (typesetting). As printed the radical bar in the stem covers 'x + 2', i.e. \(\sqrt{x+2}\) — verified by pixel measurement of the vinculum (spans the whole of x + 2, 72 px, against the 22 px vinculum the same book uses for \(\sqrt{x}\) elsewhere on the page, e.g. Ex 9.2 IV Q2). Option B carries the same over-wide bar; option D's bar correctly covers only x. Under the printed reading \(\frac{d}{dx}\frac{x-4}{\sqrt{x+2}}=\frac{x+8}{2(x+2)^{3/2}}\), which matches NO option, so the question is unanswerable as printed. The evidently-intended stem is \(y=\frac{x-4}{\sqrt{x}+2}\): then \(x-4=(\sqrt{x}-2)(\sqrt{x}+2)\) so \(y=\sqrt{x}-2\) and \(\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\) = option C, which is exactly option C as printed. Answer C is derived from that intended reading; the stem and option B are transcribed as printed, not repaired.

options.label: A
options.text: f is continuous at \(x=0\), but not differentiable at \(x=0\)

options.label: B
options.text: f is neither continuous nor differentiable at \(x=0\)

options.label: C
options.text: f is not continuous at \(x=0\), but differentiable at \(x=0\)

options.label: D
options.text: f is both continuous and differentiable at \(x=0\)

_note: BOOK DEFECT. The condition \(x\le 0\) is printed TWICE, once for each branch (verified on the page image at 2x zoom). As printed the definition is self-contradictory — it assigns two different values to every \(x\le 0\) and leaves \(f\) undefined for \(x>0\) — so the question has no answer. The evidently-intended second condition is \(x>0\). Transcribed exactly as printed, NOT repaired. The answer is derived from the intended reading: at \(x=0\) the left value is \(0+0+1=1\) and the right value is \(0-0+1=1\), so \(f\) is continuous; \(Lf'(0)=\left[2x+\cos x\right]_{x=0}=1\) while \(Rf'(0)=\left[2x-2\right]_{x=0}=-2\), so \(f\) is not differentiable at \(x=0\) — option A.
